knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Integer overflow in backend memory offset calculation for large tensors
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend kernels may calculate flattened memory offsets using integer types narrower than required by tensor numel or stride, causing silent overflow and incorrect output for very large tensors.

risk_dimensions.shape: Very large source tensor dimensions where numel or row stride can make flattened offset arithmetic exceed signed 32-bit range
risk_dimensions.dtype: Index and stride values whose product exceeds signed 32-bit integer range; backend kernels may assume narrower integer widths
risk_dimensions.memory: Flattened memory offset for selected rows exceeding INT32_MAX
risk_dimensions.device: Non-CPU backends such as MPS that may use 32-bit offset or address calculations without overflow detection
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Forward execution of index selection or embedding lookup on large tensors with backend kernel dispatch

failure_mechanism.description: The backend kernel computes a selected row memory offset as index multiplied by stride using a 32-bit integer. For large tensors, this product overflows INT32_MAX and silently produces zero or incorrect rows instead of raising an error.

input_exploration: Vary index values around the boundary where index multiplied by row stride crosses INT32_MAX
Explore large source tensors or embedding tables with numel near or above 2^31
Select valid indices that target rows immediately before and after the offset overflow boundary
Test both direct index selection APIs and embedding-style lookups with large row sizes
constraint_awareness: Backend kernels may assume offset arithmetic fits in 32-bit signed integers
Overflow depends on the product of index and row stride or row size, not only total tensor size
Silent wrong output can occur without any crash or error signal
CPU reference implementations may handle wider offsets correctly, enabling differential detection
oracle_strategy: Compare backend output against CPU or reference output for the same large-tensor indexing operation
Flag all-zero or otherwise incorrect selected rows when the reference output is nonzero
Enable integer overflow sanitizers or backend debug checks where available

transferability.reason: The risk applies broadly to APIs that perform backend address or offset calculations for large tensors, such as gather, embedding, index_select, and slicing, where hidden integer width assumptions can cause overflow.

important_considerations: Focus on combinations of large tensor numel, row size or stride, and valid indices that can overflow backend offset calculations
Use differential testing between backend and CPU reference as the main oracle
Do not limit exploration to total element count; row offset boundaries are critical
Consider backend-specific integer width assumptions in kernel implementations
generation_strategy: Generate large-tensor selection or embedding harnesses with boundary index and row-size combinations, run them on backend and CPU, and treat silent mismatches or zero rows as failure signals.
